name: ZDT, DTLZ, and WFG Multi-objective Test Suites
description: ZDT, DTLZ, and WFG are the three canonical families of scalable test problems for multi-objective evolutionary algorithms (MOEAs). ZDT (Zitzler-Deb-Thiele) provides six bi-objective problems with controllable convex, concave, and disconnected Pareto fronts. DTLZ (Deb-Thiele-Laumanns-Zitzler) scales to an arbitrary number of objectives for many-objective testing, while WFG (Walking Fish Group) adds diverse front geometries and difficult features such as bias, deception, and non-separability. Algorithms are scored by how closely and how evenly their approximation set matches the known Pareto-optimal front, using indicators like hypervolume and inverted generational distance.
evaluation_method: hypervolume / inverted generational distance (IGD) / generational distance
typical_sota_score: Algorithm-dependent; reported as indicator values against the analytically known Pareto front, with modern MOEAs (NSGA-III, MOEA/D) near-optimal on ZDT/DTLZ and challenged by WFG.
reputation: The standard synthetic test suites for multi-objective and many-objective evolutionary optimization; used in essentially every MOEA comparison.
notes: Not an LLM benchmark; synthetic test-problem families for multi-objective optimizers. Pareto fronts are known analytically, so performance is measured by convergence and diversity indicators. The three families are usually reported together to cover varied front geometries.
